name: raycast-extension-aws-vault
title: AWS Vault
description: Extension for Raycast which opens the AWS management console via aws-vault or AWS CLI.
author: sawadashota

commands.name: index
commands.title: Open AWS Console
commands.description: Opens the AWS management console via aws-vault or AWS CLI

preferences.title: aws-vault entrypoint
preferences.name: entrypoint
preferences.description: Entrypoint of aws-vault command (used with aws-vault). If default doesn't work, please set path to aws-vault.

preferences.title: AWS CLI entrypoint
preferences.name: awsCliPath
preferences.description: Entrypoint of aws command (used with AWS CLI). If default doesn't work, please set path to aws.

preferences.title: MFA Prompt
preferences.name: mfaPrompt
preferences.description: How aws-vault asks for an MFA code (used with aws-vault). "aws-vault default" respects AWS_VAULT_PROMPT.

preferences.title: aws-vault Backend
preferences.name: backend
preferences.description: Secret backend of aws-vault (--backend). Raycast does not load AWS_VAULT_BACKEND from your shell, so set it here when you don't use the keychain.

preferences.title: aws-vault Keychain
preferences.name: keychain
preferences.description: Name of the macOS keychain used by aws-vault (--keychain). Leave empty for the default.

preferences.title: aws-vault File Passphrase
preferences.name: filePassphrase
preferences.description: Passphrase of the "file" backend (AWS_VAULT_FILE_PASSPHRASE). Required with the "file" backend because aws-vault cannot prompt for it from Raycast.

preferences.title: aws-vault Touch ID
preferences.label: Use Touch ID to unlock the keychain
preferences.name: biometrics
preferences.description: Unlock the aws-vault keychain with Touch ID when it is locked (--biometrics). Requires aws-vault 7 (ByteNess) and the keychain backend. Run `aws-vault list --biometrics` in a terminal once beforehand.
